title: White audiences and 'My Blue Heaven'
summary: He finds white college kids know Domino's records and suggests recording a standard, which becomes 'My Blue Heaven'.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: And later on, when I used to get him, I started to book him in White places, in White clubs that really didn't have nothin' to do with it. And I used to go to them clubs to see him, and I used to go around and ask the kids, I mean, "Why did you come to see Domino?" Some of them said... They was college kids. They said, "Man, I've been listening to Domino since I was a kid." You know, because he had them big records that them kids used to get the money out of their parents and go... And they were fans of him but they'd never seen him. See, because up in this territory the Whites don't mix...the White clubs don't mix so much with
the Black clubs. You may see a couple of Whites in there, but you'd very seldom see a White person in a Black club... or a Black dance.
And then, later on, the guy that recorded Domino came to the office. And I told him, I said, "Why don't you record Domino on a standard?" See, I had the sense that a standard can...
Old tunes, sort of like "April in Paris" or...
So you mean tunes that are favorites of people....

Right. Right, yes. So the guy looked at me like I was crazy. And I was kind of embarrassed that I said it. I'm saying that to the guy that records him, and he's been making... On a release of Domino, he was selling 250,000 records. So who in the heck is this guy telling him what to record? I think that's what he thought. He didn't say nothin'.

About two or three months later, he came out with Domino singing "My Blue Heaven." And that record hit every radio station in the country. Because, a lot of the White jockeys at that time wasn't playing Domino's records, because he had... He had race records, you know, he had R&B

things, "Expression" and "Let Me Walk On Home" and all that stuff, which didn't attract White people. And he had a couple of tunes that a couple of White artists picked up on, but he wasn't a nationally known...
